title: Schedule Recording Terms: Value Rounding and Removal Backdating
content:
Two recording terms of the Larkspur Valuables Floater govern how the schedule itself is kept: the rounding unit for scheduled values, and how far back an item removal may be dated to a documented sale or gift.

| Tier | Scheduled values recorded rounded to (USD) | Most days a removal may be backdated to a documented sale or gift date (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|
| Valuables Floater Classic | 100 | 0 |
| Valuables Floater Select | 100 | 30 |
| Valuables Floater Preferred | 100 | 30 |
| Valuables Floater Prestige | 100 | 30 |
| Valuables Floater Collector | 50 | 60 |
| Valuables Floater Private Client | 10 | 60 |

## Notes

- **Rounding unit.** Values are recorded to the nearest multiple of the tier's unit. Hypothetical appraised value of 7340 USD: recorded as 7300 USD on the Classic, Select, Preferred or Prestige (unit 100), as 7350 USD on the Collector (unit 50), and as 7340 USD on the Private Client (unit 10).
- **Backdating allowance.** A figure of 0 on the Valuables Floater Classic means a removal there is never backdated. On the other tiers the figure is the most calendar days by which a removal may be dated back to a documented sale or gift date.
